hypothesis: E36x left one clause unresolved by the registered rule: at stride 4 the neural kernel (MDN) beats the site energy, but it selected its last checkpoint (2000) in 15 of 16 fits and none converged, so the clause could not be called, although its risk (0.020 against 0.040) is an upper bound pointing the right way. A clean-data MDN fit costs 6-15 minutes at 2000 updates, so the ladder can be extended eight-fold. E48 does that at all three strides, and also asks (Jerome's Q6: can a neural kernel be fitted by EM, and does it overfit) whether, with enough budget, it ever beats the exactly specified model.
design: The frozen e36 driver, part clean, unmodified, at other settings: arm em_mdn only; strides (1, 2, 4); seeds 0-15 (four shards of four: e48-s0, s4, s8, s12); the ladder extended to (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 120, 220, 400, 700, 1200, 2000, 3200, 5000, 8000, 12000, 16000). Comparators: E36x's frozen em_pair_quartic, em_tilted_spline and em_mixture on the same seeds and bundles (test-bundle hashes compared at read time).

predeclared_predictions.P1: Resolved: at stride 4 the MDN selects a checkpoint below the last one (16000) in at least 12 of 16 seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P2: At stride 4 the MDN's clean risk is below the site energy's in at least 14 of 16 seeds (E36x, capped: 16/16).
predeclared_predictions.P3: At stride 1, where the problem is exactly specified, the MDN stays ABOVE the site energy in 16 of 16 seeds even at 16000 updates.
predeclared_predictions.P4: At stride 1 the seed-mean ratio MDN / site energy is below 5 (E36x at 2000 updates: 5.4): more budget closes part of the gap.
predeclared_predictions.P5: At stride 2 (E36x: a tie, 0.0104 against 0.0108) the MDN is below the site energy in at least 10 of 16 seeds.

predeclared_analysis: clean.csv of the four shards; per (stride, seed) the MDN's risk against E36x's frozen em_pair_quartic; at_cap from the driver's own flag; a failed fit counts against every clause it touches; read by tools/make_extension_numbers.py.
provenance_note: Written after E36x was read (that is what motivated it) and before any E48 cell ran. P3 and P4 are judgements about what a flexible kernel does against the exactly specified one; a falsified P3 would be the more interesting outcome.
post_submission_note: Added 2026-10-09, after submission and before any E48 cell ran; the predictions are unchanged. (i) P4 quotes 'E36x at 2000 updates: 5.4' for the stride-1 MDN / site-energy ratio. That figure is 0.0103 / 0.0019, a ratio of rounded seed means. In the frozen E36x clean.csv (outputs/hpc_E36x_s0 and s8, 16 seeds) the ratio of seed means, which is the statistic the reader computes for P4 (tools/make_extension_numbers.py, read_e48), is 5.59 (0.01034 / 0.00185); the mean of the per-seed ratios is 6.47 and their median 6.04. P4's threshold (below 5) stands as registered; the E36x value it is compared with is 5.59, not 5.4. (ii) P5 calls stride 2 'a tie, 0.0104 against 0.0108'. Those are seed means; in the frozen E36x data the MDN is already below the site energy in 14 of 16 seeds at stride 2 (the exceptions are seed 0, 0.0110 against 0.0108, and seed 4, 0.0353 against 0.0107). P5's threshold (at least 10 of 16) was therefore met by the 2000-update fits before E48 ran: P5 is a non-regression check on the longer ladder, not a test.
resources: cluster, defq, 4 x 8 cpus, 24G, 10 h; a clean MDN fit took 6-15 min at 2000 updates, so up to about 2 h at 16000

outcome.read: 2026-10-10, outputs/hpc_E48_s*/clean.csv (4 shards x 12 keys), paired with E36x's frozen site-energy fits on the same seeds and test bundles, tools/make_extension_numbers.py read_e48 as pinned.
outcome.P1: FALSIFIED. Stride 4: the MDN selects a checkpoint below its last (16,000 updates) in only 5 of 16 seeds (threshold 12): even at eight times E36x's budget it is still improving, so its risks remain upper bounds.
outcome.P2: CONFIRMED. Stride 4: the MDN is below the site energy in 16 of 16 seeds; mean of per-seed ratios MDN / site energy 0.405. Since the MDN risks are upper bounds (P1), the direction is robust: under subsampling the flexible kernel beats the misspecified five-parameter one by about a factor of two and a half.
outcome.P3: CONFIRMED. Stride 1: the MDN is above the site energy in 16 of 16 seeds (mean of per-seed ratios 3.71).
outcome.P4: CONFIRMED. Stride 1: ratio of seed means MDN / site energy 2.98 (threshold 5).
outcome.P5: CONFIRMED (a non-regression check: E36x already met it, see post_submission_note). Stride 2: MDN below the site energy in 14 of 16 seeds; mean of per-seed ratios 0.913.
outcome.reading: This resolves E36x P2, left unresolved by the MDN's iteration cap: with the ladder extended to 16,000 updates the MDN is below the site energy at stride 4 in 16/16 seeds. The crossover is now measured at protocol strength: where the physics is exactly a gradient flow (stride 1) the 5-parameter site energy beats the 1,516-parameter MDN by about 3x; once subsampling takes the true kernel out of the tilted-walk class (stride 4) the MDN wins by about 2.5x; stride 2 is near the crossing. Clean-data fits only; the noisy-EM version under strides was not run.
